title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 147 (Liability of co-sureties bound in different sums)

content.overview: Section 147 provides that co-sureties who are bound in different sums are liable to pay equally as far as the limits of their respective obligations permit.
content.glance: Co-sureties bound in different sums contribute equally up to the limit of each one's obligation.
content.study: Co-sureties who are bound in different sums are liable to pay equally as far as the limits of their respective obligations permit. Current-law framing: equal contribution is applied subject to each co-surety's individual cap.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: Co-sureties who are bound in different sums are liable to pay equally as far as the limits of their respective obligations permit.

examples.title: Different limits
examples.body: One co-surety bound for 10,000 and another for 5,000. They contribute equally up to the lower limit, then the higher-bound surety bears the balance within his limit.

hypotheticals.question: Co-sureties bound for different amounts. How is contribution calculated?
hypotheticals.analysis: Under Section 147 they are liable to pay equally as far as the limits of their respective obligations permit.
